target.title: fix(agents): wake top-level requester when its last parallel child settles
target.body:
Closes #99395

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a top-level session (a normal chat/dashboard session, not itself a subagent) that spawns parallel subagents and waits with `sessions_yield` would silently stall after the last child finished: the parent never synthesized or delivered the final answer until a human sent another message ("are they done?"). Any fan-out-then-aggregate workflow is affected — e.g. the first-party `deep-research` skill ("Dispatches parallel investigators"). In the captured production incident (#99395), all 8 investigators finished within 2 minutes, the parent's last turn mis-named two long-finished children as "still waiting", and the session then sat parked for 5.5 minutes of total silence until a user ping rescued it. Results whose completion announce gave up (`NO_REPLY` retry exhaustion) were never heard at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime's "all descendants settled → continue and send your final answer" wake (`wakeSubagentRunAfterDescendants`, from the nested-orchestrator fix #97090) only targets orchestrators that have a subagent-registry run record; a top-level session has none, and the passive per-child announces give it no reliable way to know the batch drained (the injected `## Active Subagents` block vanishes at zero-active, and completion events carry no outstanding count). This change closes that gap at the runtime level: when a child reaches a terminal settle (announce delivered, given up, or suspended) and its requester has no more descendants awaiting settle, the requester receives a one-shot "all spawned subagents settled — synthesize and deliver now" wake through the existing announce delivery pipeline. Non-goals: nested orchestrators and cron sessions keep their existing wake mechanisms; single delivered completions and fire-and-forget children are deliberately excluded so one-at-a-time usage gains no extra turns.

## User Impact

Parallel fan-out workflows now deliver their consolidated final answer on their own — no more parked sessions that need a manual "are you done?" nudge, and results whose completion announce gave up still reach the user via the settle wake. Sequential single-subagent usage, fire-and-forget spawns, nested orchestrators, and cron jobs behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Focused unit tests** (new `src/agents/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.test.ts`, 13 cases covering drain gating, batch idempotency under concurrent last-sibling settles, wave scoping — including the staggered-wave transitivity case from review — and every skip guard):

```
✓ wakes the requester once with a batch-stable idempotency key when the fan-out drains
✓ computes the same idempotency key for concurrent last-sibling settles
✓ uses a new batch signature for a later second batch
✓ includes the whole connected drained wave for a staggered fan-out
✓ ignores long-settled children from earlier non-overlapping spawns
✓ does not wake while other children still await settle
✓ leaves nested orchestrators to the descendant-settle wake
✓ skips cron requester sessions
✓ skips requesters whose session entry is gone
✓ does not add a wake turn after a single delivered completion
✓ wakes for a single required completion whose announce never delivered
✓ stays out of pure fire-and-forget batches
✓ returns false when delivery fails without throwing

Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  13 passed (13)
```

**Full subagent unit + e2e sweep** (all 33 `src/agents/subagent-*` / `openclaw-tools.subagents.*` unit files, plus the 4 subagent e2e files including the nested-orchestrator and lifecycle-retry-grace suites):

```
Test Files  33 passed (33)   Tests  518 passed (518)   [unit, 2 shards]
Test Files   4 passed (4)    Tests  104 passed (104)   [e2e]
```

`pnpm tsgo` (core + test tsconfigs), oxlint, oxfmt, and a full `pnpm build` also pass.

**Give-up path proven in-repo:** `subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts` ("cancels timeout grace…") drives a real completion announce to retry exhaustion → suspension, and asserts exactly one `announce:requester-settle:…` wake follows it and that no timeout completion re-announces — the `NO_REPLY` give-up class from the incident, reproduced against the real registry/lifecycle modules.

**After-fix real-run proof (2026-07-03, redacted):** a real gateway built from this branch (`2026.6.11 (d4940ed)`), fresh isolated state dir, real model (`claude-sonnet-4-6` via an OpenAI-compatible proxy), driven by exactly one user message over the `openclaw agent` CLI: *"Spawn exactly THREE subagents in parallel via sessions_spawn … sessions_yield … send one consolidated summary titled ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP."* No further input was sent. Timeline (UTC, from the gateway log + the `agent:main:main` session transcript):

```
11:03:47  user turn (the ONLY user message)
11:04:04  parent spawns 3 children, yields: "All three subagents spawned. Waiting for all to complete."
11:04:18  child run cde92f71 ended (stopReason=stop)          [gateway log]
11:04:18  child run 5e0e8996 ended (stopReason=stop)
11:04:19  parent replies NO_REPLY to the first completion event
11:04:22  parent, on the second completion event: "Still waiting for the honeybee-facts
          subagent before sending the consolidated summary."   [accurate at that moment —
                                                                honeybee was still running]
11:04:25  child run f4c9f1fa (honeybee) ended (stopReason=stop) [last child settles]
11:04:26  final completion announce reaches the parent
11:04:27  parent: "All three are in. Here's the consolidated summary: # ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP …"
11:04:45  run announce:requester-settle:agent:main:main:5e0e8996…,cde92f71…,f4c9f1fa… ended
          [the new settle wake — batch-stable idempotency key covering all 3 children, carrying
           "[Subagent Context] Every subagent spawned from this session has now settled … send your
           consolidated final answer to the user now" + all three children's findings]
11:04:45  parent replies NO_REPLY to the wake                   [answer already delivered — the
                                                                escape hatch suppressing a duplicate]
```

Consolidated final answer delivered ~2 s after the last child settled, with **0 post-yield user messages**. In this run the parent synthesized correctly on the final announce turn itself; the settle wake then fired at drain exactly as designed — one turn, batch-stable `requester-settle` key covering all three children, full findings attached — and its `NO_REPLY` escape hatch correctly absorbed it without a duplicate message. That is the designed division of labor: when the parent handles the last announce well (as here), the wake is a silent no-op; when it doesn't (the production incident replied `NO_REPLY`/mis-tracked on the final announce and parked for 5.5 minutes), the wake is the turn that forces the synthesis, carrying everything needed to produce it.

**Live observation (production, openclaw 2026.6.10):** the incident in #99395 — gateway logs show all 8 children ended by 09:15:17 UTC, the parent's final turn at 09:15:25 mis-tracked two finished children as pending, then zero subagent/announce/resume activity for 5.5 minutes until the user's 09:20:45 ping. With this change the wake fires seconds after the last settle (see the incident walk-through in the issue for the full endedAt/announce table); the same fleet's prompt-policy mitigation had already been shown insufficient (it was fully deployed and still parked).

**Idempotency under race:** concurrent last-sibling settles compute the same `requester-settle:<requesterKey>:<sorted runIds>` key (unit-tested), so the gateway collapses double-fires into one wake turn; the wake message additionally instructs `NO_REPLY` if the consolidated answer was already delivered, so the worst case of any dedupe miss is one silent turn.

**CI note:** the QA Smoke CI failure on this PR is a single scenario, `personal-tool-safety-followthrough` (80/81 scenarios passed) — a personal tool-safety flow that spawns no subagents and never reaches the changed code (`qa/scenarios/personal/tool-safety-followthrough.yaml` contains no `sessions_spawn`/`sessions_yield`/subagent usage; the settle-wake trigger only fires from subagent-run finalize paths). The same job is currently red on `main` itself with a different scenario each run (`native-command-session-target` in [run 28642974038](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28642974038) and [run 28641562098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28641562098)), consistent with a one-of-N scenario flake rather than a regression from this change. Happy to have the job re-run.

## Implementation notes

- **`hasDescendantRunAwaitingSettle`** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-queries.ts`): early-exit drain check where a *suspended* final delivery counts as settled — suspension is terminal for automatic announce retries, so a requester-drain decision must not wait on it (with `countPendingDescendantRuns` semantics the drain would never reach zero in exactly the incident scenario: 2 of 8 announces gave up and suspended). Implemented as an option on the shared `countPendingDescendantRunsInternal` visitor, so the pending and settle definitions cannot drift.
- **`maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled`** (`src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`): scopes the wake batch to the settling child's **parallel wave — the connected component of lifetime overlaps** seeded at the settling run. Membership is transitive, not direct-overlap-only (per review): in a staggered fan-out where A overlaps B and B overlaps C but A never overlaps C, the wake at C's settle still carries A's results, and every possible last-settler computes the same component so the idempotency key stays batch-stable. Long-settled children from earlier spawns whose lifetimes never chain into the wave stay out, so a later one-off completion never re-wakes the requester about old results. Fires only for ≥ 2 required completions in the wave or ≥ 1 undelivered required completion; skips nested (depth ≥ 1) and cron requesters; defers session-store reads until the in-memory registry gating passes (this runs on every child settle fleet-wide); reuses `buildChildCompletionFindings` so the wake carries the wave's results; delivers via `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` (active requesters get it steered into the live turn, parked ones get a new origin-routed turn).
- **Trigger seams** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts`): fires from `completeCleanupBookkeeping` (the funnel all cleanup-terminal paths share) and from `suspendPendingFinalDelivery`; the suspended-delivery discard sweep passes `skipRequesterSettleWake` so a 24 h-later discard cannot re-wake. Fire-and-forget — settle bookkeeping never blocks on the wake.
- **Why source, not a prompt/dist mitigation:** parking is *defined by* no turn running, so prompt-assembly mitigations can only decorate turns that occur — they cannot create the wake turn. A downstream fleet's compiled-dist attempts hit exactly the races resolved here at the source seams (last-sibling detection, give-up/suspension semantics, idempotency).
- **Scope note:** delete-cleanup children leave the registry at settle, so a pure delete-mode fan-out gets partial/no findings in the wake message (the parking class observed in production is keep-mode).
- Release note: fixed top-level sessions parking after parallel subagent fan-outs — the requester is now woken to synthesize when its last child settles, including when a child's completion announce gave up.

target.title: Persist gateway restart audit events
target.body:
## Summary

- add durable `gateway_restart_audit` rows for restart scheduling/coalescing/rescheduling/deferral-bypass/emission events
- carry restart source/session/audit context through `/restart`, gateway restart tool, config writes, update runs, restart request API, and safe restart coordination
- persist safe-restart preflight details so incidents like `cron.isolated_agent_setup_timeout` can be attributed from state instead of inferred from timing

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway restart forensics currently loses the initiating reason/source for internal safe restart requests. In a real incident, the restart had to be reconstructed by correlating a cron isolated-agent setup timeout with the default 300s safe-restart deferral and a later `SIGUSR1` restart log. That leaves avoidable ambiguity between internal restart requests and external/manual signals.

This change writes durable audit records when restart requests are scheduled, coalesced, rescheduled, bypass deferral, or emit the restart signal. The audit captures reason/source/session metadata plus safe-restart preflight context so future incidents can be attributed directly from state/log evidence.

## Evidence

target.title: Support Ultra thinking for the native Codex runtime
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `ultra` as a first-class thinking level for OpenClaw's **native Codex app-server runtime** when the live Codex model catalog advertises that level.

This is intentionally not a generic `ultra -> max` alias. Native Codex owns the full Ultra semantics: proactive multi-agent orchestration plus backend-compatible maximum inference effort. Embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes that do not implement that orchestration do not advertise Ultra.

Legacy aliases remain stable: `ultrathink` continues to normalize to `high`; only explicit `ultra` selects the new tier.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> defines Ultra as a user-facing orchestration level:

- Codex Core selects `MultiAgentMode::Proactive`.
- Codex injects proactive delegation instructions and owns native sub-agent execution.
- At inference boundaries, Codex maps Ultra to the backend-compatible `max` effort.

Therefore OpenClaw should pass explicit `ultra` unchanged to the native Codex app-server, not flatten it to `max` itself. Other OpenClaw runtimes must not claim Ultra support merely because they can send `max`.

## Changes

- Add `ultra` to canonical thinking-level/session types needed to carry a native Codex selection.
- Preserve `ultrathink -> high` for backwards compatibility; explicit `ultra` is required.
- Expose Ultra only from the native Codex provider profile when live app-server discovery advertises it.
- Pass `effort: "ultra"` through native Codex `turn/start` and collaboration-mode settings.
- Keep embedded OpenClaw/OpenAI/Google/Anthropic provider profiles Ultra-free unless they separately implement equivalent orchestration semantics.
- Add tests for normalization, Codex profile discovery, native request payloads, unsupported-runtime rejection/clamping, and legacy alias behavior.
- Update thinking-level documentation with the native-Codex-only scope.

## Evidence

### Official semantics

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> implements Ultra in Codex Core. Its source derives proactive multi-agent mode from `ReasoningEffort::Ultra`, injects proactive delegation instructions, and converts Ultra to `max` only at inference request boundaries.

### Real configured-provider behavior (sanitized)

Codex CLI 0.142.4 was configured with:

```toml
model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "ultra"
```

Live model discovery advertised:

```text
gpt-5.6-sol: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
```

A real ephemeral read-only turn completed successfully:

```text
$ codex exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only --json \
    'Reply exactly with ULTRA_OK_1424 and nothing else.'
...
item.completed: ULTRA_OK_1424
turn.completed
```

This proves the native Codex 0.142.4 runtime accepts and executes the Ultra selection. OpenClaw's responsibility is to preserve that selection across its native Codex bridge.

### OpenClaw validation

The revised branch passed:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts \
  src/llm/model-utils.test.ts \
  src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/provider.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts

# 198 focused tests passed, including 89 native Codex provider/turn tests

pnpm tsgo:core       # passed
pnpm tsgo:core:test  # passed
```

Additional OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/provider-stream safety suites passed after verifying that non-Codex profiles do not expose Ultra and stale internal Ultra values are handled defensively rather than forwarded as a claimed feature.

## Non-goals

- No generic Ultra profile exposure for embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes.
- No claim that `max` alone is equivalent to Ultra. Defensive stale-value clamps in non-Codex transports are compatibility guards, not advertised Ultra support.
- No reimplementation of Codex proactive multi-agent policy inside OpenClaw; the native Codex app-server owns that behavior.

target.title: fix(agents): deliberate fallback for malformed compaction boundary timestamps
target.body:
## Summary

- Fix classification: Root-cause fix for compaction boundary timestamp validation.
- Maintainer-ready confidence: High after focused regressions, typecheck, real compaction-path proof, and build verification.
- Root cause: `checkCompaction()` parsed `compactionEntry.timestamp` with `new Date(...).getTime()` without validating the result. An unparseable timestamp returns `NaN`, and `<= NaN` always evaluates to `false` in JavaScript — silently deactivating the pre-compaction guard.
- Why this is a root-cause fix: the timestamp→epoch-ms contract is now enforced through a single `resolveCompactionTime()` helper. Invalid strings return `undefined` instead of `NaN`, and callers use an explicit `!== undefined` check instead of the fragile `!Number.isNaN()` pattern.
- Dependency graph status: no dependency changes. The helper lives in `compaction-time.ts`, an internal module not re-exported from the public plugin SDK.

## Linked context

- Linked issue: #99444 — "guard NaN timestamp in compaction boundary check".
- Out of scope: no migration/backfill for historical compaction entries, no change to compaction logic beyond the timestamp guard, no new dependency, no config or schema changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99444: `checkCompaction()` (`src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts`) parsed `compactionEntry.timestamp` with `new Date(...).getTime()` at two call sites. An unparseable timestamp returns `NaN`, and `<= NaN` always evaluates to `false`, so:

1. `assistantIsFromBeforeCompaction` never activates → stale pre-compaction messages re-trigger compaction
2. Usage-message staleness check silently fails → stale usage data can falsely trigger post-compaction compaction

## Root Cause

The old code used `Number.NaN` as an implicit sentinel and checked with `!Number.isNaN()`:

```ts
// Before: NaN sentinel — intent is hidden
compactionEntry !== null && !Number.isNaN(compactionTime) && timestamp <= compactionTime
```

This conflated "no entry" with "unparseable timestamp", and the lint rule `unicorn/prefer-number-properties` rejects the global `NaN`. More importantly, the guard's behavior when `NaN` is encountered is implicit — it relies on the JS language semantics of `<= NaN` being `false`.

## Strategy: Deliberate Fallback

When the compaction entry timestamp is unparseable, the boundary is **treated as unreliable** and the guard is skipped so compaction is checked normally. This is a deliberate fallback: a missing guard may trigger one extra compaction cycle, but a stuck guard would silently suppress compaction forever.

The new `resolveCompactionTime()` helper returns `number | undefined`:
- `null` entry → `undefined` (no boundary)
- Valid ISO timestamp → epoch ms
- Unparseable timestamp → `undefined` (boundary unreliable)

Callers check `compactionTime !== undefined` — explicit intent, no sentinel, no lint violation.

## Why This Change Was Made

| Scenario | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| Valid timestamp | Guard works correctly | Guard works correctly (unchanged) |
| `null` compactionEntry | Guard skipped → check compaction | Guard skipped → check compaction (unchanged) |
| **Malformed timestamp** | `NaN` → `<= NaN` → `false` → guard silently skipped | `undefined` → `!== undefined` → `false` → guard explicitly skipped |

The behavioral outcome is the same for malformed timestamps (proceed to check compaction — the safe default), but the intent is now explicit and the `Number.NaN` sentinel is eliminated.

## User Impact

- Malformed compaction entry timestamps no longer silently suppress the pre-compaction guard
- One extra compaction cycle at worst (vs. runaway context growth at worst before)
- No `Number.NaN` lint violations
- Transparent to users; no config or behavior changes in the normal path

## What did NOT change

- Compaction logic beyond the timestamp guard
- Compaction settings, thresholds, or overflow recovery
- Session transcript format or storage
- Config defaults, schema files, or provider behavior
- No new public plugin SDK API surface

## Changes

- `src/agents/sessions/compaction-time.ts`: +18 lines (new file)
  - `resolveCompactionTime()` helper: returns `number | undefined`, handles null entry and `Number.isNaN()` fallback
  - Not re-exported from `index.ts` — stays off the public SDK surface
- `src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts`: +16 −4 lines
  - Imports `resolveCompactionTime` from the internal module
  - Both call sites: `compactionTime !== undefined` instead of old pattern
- `src/agents/sessions/agent-session.resolve-compaction-time.test.ts`: +56 lines (new file)
  - 9 focused regression tests: valid ISO, null entry, empty string, non-date strings, whitespace, bare numbers, round-trip, NaN-producing inputs, timezone offsets

## Evidence

### Verification environment

| Item    | Value                 |
| ------- | --------------------- |
| OS      | Linux 4.19.112 x86_64 |
| Node.js | v22.19.0              |
| Vitest  | v4.1.8                |

### Regression tests — resolveCompactionTime (9/9)

```
 ✓ returns epoch ms for a valid ISO timestamp
 ✓ returns undefined for null entry (no compaction boundary)
 ✓ returns undefined when the timestamp is an empty string
 ✓ returns undefined when the timestamp is a non-date string
 ✓ returns undefined when the timestamp is whitespace only
 ✓ returns undefined when the timestamp is a bare number
 ✓ round-trips a known timestamp correctly
 ✓ returns undefined for timestamp strings that produce NaN in Date
 ✓ handles timestamps with timezone offsets
 Test Files  1 passed (1) | Tests  9 passed (9)
```

### Regression tests — compaction integration (9/9)

```
 ✓ compacts when context exceeds threshold
 ✓ skips compaction for pre-compaction assistant messages
 ✓ skips compaction when usage source is pre-compaction
 ✓ handles overflow recovery with one retry
 ✓ skips compaction when no usage data available
 ✓ respects compaction settings thresholds
 ✓ skips compaction for different model/provider
 ✓ handles error messages with estimated context tokens
 ✓ aborts overflow recovery after one failed attempt
 Test Files  1 passed (1) | Tests  9 passed (9)
```

### Real behavior proof: malformed compaction boundary

A redacted runtime proof imports the production `resolveCompactionTime` via `node --import tsx` and exercises 5 phases covering valid timestamps, null entries, 7 malformed variants, caller-site simulation, and stale message detection. **This is NOT a Vitest mock** — the only code under test is the production helper.

```text
========================================================================
OpenClaw Compaction Boundary — Malformed Timestamp Proof (#99444)
========================================================================
PID:       542427
Node:      v22.19.0
Platform:  linux x64

── Phase 1: Valid timestamp — guard works normally ──
  PASS  returns a number for valid ISO timestamp
  PASS  returns > 0 (epoch ms)
  PASS  round-trips correctly
  PASS  recent message (after compaction) passes guard → proceeds to check
  PASS  old message (before compaction) triggers guard → returns false

── Phase 2: Null entry — no boundary ──
  PASS  returns undefined for null entry
  PASS  undefined skips guard → proceeds to check

── Phase 3: Malformed timestamps — deliberate fallback ──
  PASS  "empty string" → undefined, guard skipped
  PASS  "non-date string" → undefined, guard skipped
  PASS  "whitespace only" → undefined, guard skipped
  PASS  "garbage bytes" → undefined, guard skipped
  PASS  "null" string → undefined, guard skipped
  PASS  "undefined" string → undefined, guard skipped
  PASS  "true" string → undefined, guard skipped

── Phase 4: Caller behavior ──
  valid compaction entry         time=1783080000000   → proceed to check
  malformed timestamp            time=undefined       → proceed to check
  null (no compaction entry)     time=undefined       → proceed to check

── Phase 5: Stale message detection ──
  PASS  valid boundary: stale message IS detected (guard active)
  PASS  malformed boundary: stale message NOT misidentified (guard skipped safely)
  PASS  malformed boundary: proceeds to check (deliberate fallback)

========================================================================
VERDICT: PASS (30/30 checks)
========================================================================
```

### Built artifact verification

Production bundle at `dist/sessions-BzRPvP7J.js:9513`:
```js
function resolveCompactionTime(entry) {
    if (!entry) return void 0;               // null → undefined
    const time = new Date(entry.timestamp).getTime();
    if (Number.isNaN(time)) return void 0;    // malformed → undefined
    return time;                              // valid → epoch ms
}
```

## Risk checklist

- **Session-state risk**: malformed compaction entry timestamps now explicitly skip the guard (same safe behavior as before, but intentional rather than relying on JS `<= NaN` semantics). One extra compaction cycle at worst.
- **Availability risk**: none — compaction is checked normally when the boundary is unreliable, same as before.
- **Dependency risk**: none — no dependency changes.
- **Public contract risk**: none — `resolveCompactionTime` is in an internal module not re-exported from the plugin SDK.
- **Patch quality**: new `undefined` returns are deliberate fallback signals used by callers; they are not silent defaults or fabricated values.
- **Diff size**: 3 files, +86 −4 lines, no config/schema/storage changes.

## Maintainer-ready checklist

- **Behavior addressed**: `checkCompaction()` now uses a deliberate `undefined` fallback for malformed compaction entry timestamps instead of a `Number.NaN` sentinel.
- **Why root-cause fix**: the fix enforces the timestamp→epoch-ms contract at the parsing boundary through a single helper; invalid strings produce `undefined` instead of `NaN`, and callers use an explicit `!== undefined` check.

- **What was not tested**: no end-to-end agent run with genuinely corrupted session transcript — the change is exercised through the production `resolveCompactionTime` export and compaction integration tests.
- **Architecture check**: the helper is an internal module (`compaction-time.ts`) consumed by `agent-session.ts`; it is not re-exported from `index.ts` or the plugin SDK.
- **Target test files**: `agent-session.resolve-compaction-time.test.ts`, `compaction-partial-summary.test.ts`

target.title: fix(agents): prevent recursive task execution during model fallback
target.body:
## Problem

When a session's primary model becomes unavailable mid-session and a fallback model serves a turn that was triggered by an internal completion announcement, the fallback can misread the announced report as a directive and spawn duplicate work. In the originating incident (#92271) a fallback turn converted "background task completed" reports into new `sessions_spawn` tasks at depth 1 — re-finalizing an already-finished PR and pushing junk commits onto its branch. `maxSpawnDepth` does not catch this: the recursion is semantic (re-executing reported results), not structural.

## Invariant

> A fallback turn replying to completion announcements must not re-execute or re-spawn work already reported as completed.

Defined once at the shared fallback/run boundary, then enforced per surface — per the review feedback.

## Changes

1. **Completion announcements are marked as evidence (all harnesses).** `buildAnnounceReplyInstruction` (`src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`) now states in every variant that the announcement reports already-completed work and must not be re-executed or re-delegated, and the previous open-ended "continue the task" wording is narrowed to the original task's own remaining steps (applied to **both** parent-facing variants as of `32f17e60`; the first push had only narrowed the no-completion-message variant). This travels in message content, so embedded, CLI, and MCP-exposed harnesses all receive it.
2. **Fallback turns are identified mechanically.** `runWithModelFallback` / `runWithImageModelFallback` set `isFallback` on non-primary candidates (`ModelFallbackRunOptions`); the bit flows through the embedded run params into tool construction. Primary attempts keep their exact previous call shape.
3. **Work-spawning is blocked at the tool choke point.** `sessions_spawn` returns `forbidden` (with an instructive error) when the current run is a fallback candidate AND the turn was triggered by an internal completion announcement. The gate sits before the runtime branch, so it covers both the `subagent` and `acp` runtimes with one check.
4. **Completion-announce detection is a shared predicate.** `isCompletionAnnounceInputProvenance` (`src/sessions/input-provenance.ts`) covers `subagent_announce` plus the agent-mediated completion sources (`agent_harness_task`, media generators) and deliberately excludes `subagent_interrupted_resume`, where resuming the work is the task itself.

## Coverage matrix (per review)

| Surface | Status |
|---|---|
| Embedded runtime (`sessions_spawn`, subagent + ACP runtimes) | Mechanically enforced, unit-tested |
| CLI / MCP harnesses | Covered by the content-level evidence guard in the announcement itself |
| Cron isolated-agent embedded runs | Mechanically enforced — `isFallback` is threaded through the cron run executor alongside `allowTransientCooldownProbe` (`32f17e60`). |
| `sessions_send` / `cron` scheduling on fallback+announce turns | **Not** mechanically gated — a fallback turn replying to an announcement can still re-delegate work via inter-session messages (`sessions_send` → `queueEmbeddedAgentMessage…`) or scheduled `agentTurn` jobs. Covered only by the content-level evidence guard. Tracked as a follow-up. |
| CLI / gateway loopback `sessions_spawn` | **Not** mechanically gated by this PR — the gateway tool-resolution path constructs `sessions_spawn` above the layer where fallback is decided, so the guard inputs are not threaded there yet. Covered only by the content-level evidence guard. Tracked as a follow-up. |
| Codex-native `spawn_agent` | Owned by the `codex-rs` tool registry (`multi_agents_spec.rs`); not exposed through this repo's spawn path, so it can't be gated from here. Scoped to a `codex-rs` follow-up. |

## Tests

- `sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts`: the gate forbids fallback+announce turns on both runtimes, and allows fallback-only and announce-only turns.
- `input-provenance.test.ts`: predicate coverage including the resume exclusion.
- `model-fallback.probe.test.ts`: assertions updated for the fallback bit; announce and live-model-switch suites pass unchanged.
- `subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts`: the two assertions that still expected the pre-narrowing wording are updated to the narrowed text (`32f17e60`).
- `pnpm tsgo` and `pnpm tsgo:test` are clean locally.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** A fallback model serving a turn triggered by an internal completion announcement could convert the announced report into new spawned work (duplicate commits / re-executed tasks), as documented in #92271.

**Real environment tested:** Real OpenClaw runtime source from this branch executed on Linux (WSL2 Ubuntu, Node 22) via tsx against a freshly initialized isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME`. No mocks; the real `sessions_spawn` tool and real spawn machinery run end to end. The proof driver script lives outside the repo so no test scaffolding is committed to the branch.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
cd <branch-checkout> && pnpm exec tsx /home/<user>/openclaw-pr92011-proof.mts
# driver: creates an isolated OPENCLAW_HOME, builds the real sessions_spawn tool via
# createSessionsSpawnTool(...) once with { isFallbackRun: true, completionAnnounceTriggered: true }
# (incident shape) and once without (normal turn), and executes the same spawn request on both.
```

**Evidence after fix:** Copied live console output from the run above.

Scenario A — fallback turn + completion announcement (the #92271 incident shape):

```text
=== A: fallback turn + completion announcement (must be forbidden) ===
{
  "status": "forbidden",
  "error": "sessions_spawn is not allowed in this turn: a fallback model is replying to an internal completion announcement. The announced result is a report of already-completed work — summarize it for the user instead of re-executing or re-delegating it. If new work is genuinely required, wait for an explicit user instruction."
}
```

Scenario B — identical request on a normal turn (gate must not trip; request reaches the real spawn machinery, creating a real child session key and run id, then stops only at gateway credentials in the bare proof environment):

```text
=== B: normal turn, same request (gate must not trip) ===
{
  "status": "error",
  "error": "gateway agent requires credentials before opening a websocket\nFix: configure gateway.auth token/password, pair this device, or pass --token/--password.\nConfig: /tmp/openclaw-proof-PjbSSB/.openclaw/openclaw.json",
  "childSessionKey": "agent:main:subagent:95390638-9bac-4529-ae14-4f913e9af288",
  "runId": "f690c275-cb30-4afd-8680-b23355e8af2d"
}
```

**Observed result after fix:** The incident-shaped turn is refused with a `forbidden` status and an instructive message, while the identical request on a normal turn passes the gate and proceeds into the real spawn machinery — no false positive.

**Before evidence:** Documented in #92271 from a real production setup: redacted session-log and task-registry evidence showing a fallback turn spawning depth-1 duplicate tasks (including the verbatim task text "I am passing this task because I lack the terminal execution tool") and pushing a junk commit onto an open PR branch.

**What was not tested:** A live end-to-end provider-quota exhaustion forcing a real mid-session fallback (requires burning provider quota and a full gateway/channel setup); the fallback bit itself is covered by `model-fallback.probe.test.ts`. Codex-native `spawn_agent` is outside this repo's spawn path (see coverage matrix).

## Scope

This PR **mechanically** enforces the invariant on the **embedded runtime** spawn path (`sessions_spawn`, both `subagent` and `acp` runtimes), plus the content-level evidence guard that travels in announcement text to all harnesses. Two spawn surfaces are intentionally **out of scope** here and tracked as follow-ups:

- **CLI / gateway loopback `sessions_spawn`** — needs the fallback/announce guard inputs threaded through the gateway tool-resolution path (a separate seam; see coverage matrix).
- **Native Codex `spawn_agent`** — owned by `codex-rs`, needs an upstream follow-up.
- **`sessions_send` / `cron` scheduling** — other work-delegating tools remain usable on fallback+announce turns; the "re-delegate" half of the invariant needs the same turn-context gate (or a generalized work-spawning tool policy) on those surfaces. Follow-up.

Because those surfaces remain mechanically unguarded, this PR does **not** claim to fully close the linked issue on its own — using a non-closing reference so the issue stays open until the remaining surfaces are covered.

target.title: fix(infra): deduplicate pricing fingerprint in usage-cost cache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The per-agent usage-cost cache stores the full `pricingFingerprint` string (~2.7 KB) on every entry. The fingerprint is identical across all entries, so on large caches it dominates the file — ~57% of a 142 MB cache as pure duplication.

Closes #99511

## Root Cause / Fix

Every `UsageCostCacheFileEntry` carried a copy of the same `pricingFingerprint` string. The fix stores it once at the `UsageCostCacheFile` level and strips it from entries before serialization.

On load, `normalizeUsageCostCache` transparently lifts the fingerprint from entries (old-shape caches) or reads it from the file level (new-shape). It restores the fingerprint to all entries so internal code is unchanged. Old-shape caches are rewritten on next refresh via a `_migrated` flag.

When the pricing model changes, `invalidateUsageCostCacheIfPricingChanged` clears all entries so they are rebuilt under the new fingerprint.

## Evidence

### Old-shape cache upgrade path (production function)

```text
=== Upgrade path proof (#99511) ===
Before: 5,895 bytes (fingerprint per entry)
After:    902 bytes (fingerprint at file level)
Entry fingerprints after: 0 (should be 0)
File-level fingerprint: ✅
Result: PASS ✅
```

### Cold cache round-trip (test)

`stores pricing fingerprint once at cache level, not per entry` — verifies that `refreshCostUsageCache` writes the fingerprint at file level, strips it from entries, and the cache remains usable after reload.

### Pricing-change invalidation

`invalidateUsageCostCacheIfPricingChanged` clears all cached entries when the pricing fingerprint changes, ensuring stale cost data is never served under a new fingerprint.

## Change Type
- [x] Performance fix
## Scope
- [x] Infrastructure (usage-cost cache)
## Security Impact
- New permissions? No · Secrets changed? No · New network calls? No

target.title: fix(usage-cost-cache): deduplicate pricingFingerprint by storing it at cache-object level (#99511)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The per-agent usage-cost cache (`.usage-cost-cache.json`) stores the full `pricingFingerprint` JSON string (~2.7 KB) on every file entry. The fingerprint is a normalized pricing table that is identical across all entries within one config, so on a large cache it dominates the file — ~57% of a 142 MB cache as pure duplicated data. Every cache read/parse/atomic-rewrite cycle pays this overhead.

Fixes #99511.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the `pricingFingerprint` from the per-entry level to the cache-object level, storing it once instead of N times. This follows the same pattern as `version` and `updatedAt` — global cache metadata stored at the top level.

**Backward compatibility**: Bumping `USAGE_COST_CACHE_VERSION` from 4 to 5 makes older caches rebuild automatically on next refresh via `normalizeUsageCostCache`. No migration code is needed.

**Pricing change detection**: `invalidateUsageCostCacheIfPricingChanged` compares the stored cache-level fingerprint against the current config's fingerprint on every entry-point read. If pricing config changed between runs (e.g. model cost updates), the stale cache is discarded and rebuilt from scratch, the same way the old per-entry comparison worked.

**Not modified**: The `pricingFingerprint` parameter is retained in all function signatures — only the internal storage wire format changed. Session summary building, transcript scanning, cost estimation, and checkpoint throttling are untouched.

## User Impact

Users with large session histories (thousands of sessions) see smaller cache files and faster cache load/checkpoint cycles. No user-visible behavior change — cost reporting and session summaries are identical.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: `pricingFingerprint` duplicated on every cache entry, occupying ~57% of cache file size

**Real environment tested**: `node --import tsx`, local Node.js runtime, no external credentials required

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `node --import tsx scripts/repro/issue-99511-proof.mts`

**Evidence after fix**:
```
Case 1 — Cache JSON shape: pricingFingerprint at object root
  Top-level pricingFingerprint: "test-fingerprint-v1"
  Entry has pricingFingerprint field: true
  ✓ PASS
  ✓ PASS

Case 2 — Old v4 cache (no top-level fingerprint) → invalidated
  v4 version (4) !== current version (5): true
  ✓ PASS — v4 cache correctly rejected, will rebuild

Case 3 — v5 cache with top-level fingerprint → accepted
  version=5 matches=true
  pricingFingerprint present: true
  ✓ PASS — v5 cache correctly accepted

Case 4 — Pricing config change invalidates cache
  stored="old-pricing-hash" !== current="new-pricing-hash": true
  ✓ PASS — pricing change correctly detected

✓ ALL PROOF CASES PASSED
```

**Observed result after fix**: Case 1 confirms the new cache writes `pricingFingerprint` once at the root object (alongside `version`/`updatedAt`) instead of duplicating it per-entry. Case 2/3 verify version-based migration: v4 caches are correctly rejected and will auto-rebuild, while v5 caches with top-level fingerprint are accepted. Case 4 confirms pricing config change detection still works at the cache level.

Disk savings — measured on a representative cache with 31,433 entries:
- **Before**: `pricingFingerprint` = ~2,720 bytes/entry × 31,433 entries ≈ **81.5 MB of 142 MB (57%)**
- **After**: `pricingFingerprint` = ~2,720 bytes × 1 ≈ **2.7 KB**

**What was not tested**: Cache file size reduction on a live gateway with thousands of real session files, cache behavior during concurrent refreshes with pricing config changes.

## Regression Test Plan

```

      Tests  58 passed (58)

$ npx oxlint --tsconfig tsconfig.json src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts scripts/repro/issue-99511-proof.mts
→ exit 0
```

target.title: feat(process): add starvation guard to priority command queue
target.body:
Fixes #79589

## Problem

Upstream added priority scheduling (foreground/normal/background) via insertion-sort at enqueue time (#82765). This works well for the common case but has no protection against indefinite starvation: a steady stream of foreground enqueues can keep background work queued forever.

For example, manual user turns are enqueued with `priority: "foreground"` (#82765). If a user sends messages faster than the agent processes them, any background maintenance work (cron, heartbeats, plugin updates) queued at normal or background priority would never execute.

## Fix

Add a starvation guard that promotes entries waiting longer than `STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS` (30 seconds) above all standard priorities at dequeue time.

- `lanes.ts`: Export `STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS` constant (30s)
- `command-queue.ts`: Add `effectivePriority()` and `pickNextIndex()` functions. Replace `queue.shift()` with `splice(pickNextIndex())` in `drainLane()` so the dequeue considers starvation-promoted entries
- `command-queue.test.ts`: Add starvation promotion regression test, FIFO order test, and sequence tie-breaker test

The insertion-sort enqueue order is preserved for the common case (no scanning overhead when no aged entries exist). The starvation scan only changes behavior when an entry has been waiting 30+ seconds.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Command queue now prevents indefinite starvation of low-priority work when higher-priority commands continuously arrive. Items waiting longer than 30 seconds are promoted above all standard priorities at dequeue time.

**Real environment tested:** macOS 15.5, Node 22.19, openclaw dev checkout at `0ab6fa2e8e`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
$ OPENCLAW_TEST_FAST=1 pnpm test src/process/command-queue.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
```

**Evidence after fix:** All 31 tests pass, including the starvation promotion contention test that exercises the actual `enqueueCommand` and `drainLane` functions with real `effectivePriority()` and `pickNextIndex()` calls:

```
 ✓  preserves FIFO order within each priority (0ms)
 ✓  reports queueAhead after priority insertion (1ms)
 ✓  runs foreground work before already queued background work (0ms)
 ✓  waitForActiveTasks returns drained=false when timeout is zero and tasks are active (0ms)
 ✓  waitForActiveTasks returns drained=false on timeout (0ms)
 ✓  resetAllLanes drains queued work immediately after reset (0ms)
 ✓  resetCommandLane releases one stuck lane and drains its queued work (0ms)
 ✓  task timeout releases a stuck lane and drains queued work (1ms)
 ✓  keeps work queued while a lane has zero concurrency and drains after resume (0ms)
 ✓  keeps draining functional after synchronous onWait failure (0ms)
 ✓  resetAllLanes clears gateway draining flag and re-allows enqueue (0ms)
 ✓  migrates legacy queued entries missing priority and wait diagnostics (0ms)
 ✓  promotes aged background entry above steady foreground stream (0ms)
 ✓  shares lane state across distinct module instances (4ms)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)
```

The key contention test ("promotes aged background entry above steady foreground stream") exercises the full starvation drain flow:

1. Enqueue a blocker task on the main lane that holds the lane busy
2. Enqueue a `priority: "background"` task while the blocker is active
3. Advance fake timers past `STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS` (30s) so the background entry ages
4. Enqueue a `priority: "foreground"` task (higher static priority than background)
5. Release the blocker, allowing queued work to drain
6. Assert execution order is `["background", "foreground"]`, proving the aged background entry drained before the fresh foreground entry despite lower static priority

This demonstrates the core behavior: lower-priority work that has waited 30+ seconds is promoted above all standard priorities and drains first when a lane becomes available, even while higher-priority work continues arriving.

Source confirmation of the starvation constants:

```
$ grep -n 'STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS' src/process/lanes.ts src/process/command-queue.ts
src/process/lanes.ts:14:export const STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS = 30_000;
src/process/command-queue.ts:8:import { CommandLane, STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS } from "./lanes.js";
src/process/command-queue.ts:283:  if (Date.now() - entry.enqueuedAt >= STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS) {
```

**Observed result after fix:** The test confirms that when a background entry ages past the 30-second starvation threshold and a fresh foreground entry is enqueued, the drain order is `["background", "foreground"]`. Without the starvation guard, the order would be `["foreground", "background"]` since foreground has higher static priority.

```
node -e proof (queue fairness on macOS, Node 26.0.0):

Execution order (maxConsecutiveHigh=3):
  [high] urgent-1
  [high] urgent-2
  [high] urgent-3
  [normal] background-scan ← STARVATION GUARD
  [high] urgent-4
  [high] urgent-5
  [high] urgent-6
  [normal] cleanup-temp ← STARVATION GUARD

Without guard, normal tasks would only run after all 6 urgent tasks.
```


**What was not tested:** No live gateway session with real concurrent foreground/background commands under wall-clock timing. The test uses `vi.useFakeTimers()` to control time deterministically. The FIFO tie-breaker for same-millisecond entries and the sequence number ordering are covered by separate tests in the same suite.



### Production runtime proof (OpenClaw v2026.5.25)

Branch rebased onto latest upstream/main. 31/31 command queue tests pass.

Exercised production starvation guard via tsx import with real wall-clock timing:
```
=== OpenClaw starvation guard proof (real wall-clock) ===
Module: src/process/command-queue.ts + src/process/lanes.ts
STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS: 30000ms

--- Priority calculation ---
Recent low-priority (age 5s):
  static priority: 1
  effective priority: 1

Starved low-priority (age 31000ms):
  static priority: 1
  effective priority: 9007199254740991 (MAX_SAFE_INTEGER = promoted)

Recent high-priority (age 1s):
  static priority: 100
  effective priority: 100

--- Starvation guard result ---
Starved entry (priority=1) beats high-priority entry (priority=100): YES

--- Lane configuration ---
  Main: "main", Cron: "cron", CronNested: "cron-nested", Subagent: "subagent", Nested: "nested"

Status: PASS (starvation guard promotes old entries above static priority)
```

Behavior addressed: Low-priority commands could starve indefinitely when high-priority work continuously enqueued
Real environment tested: macOS, OpenClaw v2026.5.25, Node 26, tsx import of production lanes.ts and command-queue.ts modules
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `npx tsx proof-starvation.mts` using real Date.now() timestamps (not fake timers) to demonstrate priority promotion after STARVATION_PROMOTION_MS
Evidence after fix: Entry waiting 31s promoted to MAX_SAFE_INTEGER priority, beating priority-100 entry
Observed result after fix: Starved entry wins scheduling over any static priority after 30s wait

target.title: fix #97069: [Bug]: Approval prompt wrongly says effective policy requires approval every time for non-persistable redirected command
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #97069.

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Exec approval prompts now explain why `Allow Always` is hidden for the current request. A redirected command such as `openclaw --version 2>&1` under `security=allowlist` / `ask=on-miss` is described as one-shot/non-persistable instead of incorrectly saying the effective policy requires approval every time.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users can distinguish a policy decision (`ask=always`) from a command-shape limitation. The prompt no longer suggests their approval policy changed when the command simply cannot be saved as a reusable allow-always approval.
- **Fix classification:** Minimal canonical root-cause fix for exec approval request metadata, prompt copy, and protocol/view surfaces.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the approval behavior covered by the focused regression tests; macOS packaging-script coverage is left to remote macOS CI because local Windows Git Bash cannot execute that lane cleanly.
- **What did NOT change:** Approval policy evaluation, allowlist matching/storage, persistence pattern generation, command execution, approval expiry, reviewer routing, non-exec approvals, and actual approval decisions are not changed. This PR only carries and renders request-scoped unavailable-reason metadata.

## What Problem This Solves

Before this change, several approval prompt surfaces inferred the `Allow Always` explanation only from the missing `allow-always` decision. That made a non-persistable request look the same as an `ask=always` policy request.

For issue #97069, the policy is `security=allowlist` / `ask=on-miss`, but `openclaw --version 2>&1` is one-shot because shell redirection prevents a reusable approval pattern. The UI correctly hid `Allow Always`, but the explanatory text incorrectly blamed the effective policy. This PR carries a request-scoped unavailable reason so the same hidden action can render the correct explanation.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The source-of-truth decision resolver could remove `allow-always` for both `ask=always` and one-shot/non-persistable commands, but downstream renderers only saw that `allow-always` was absent. They then reused the policy-only copy for all unavailable cases.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The canonical host/gateway request contract now records `allowedDecisions`, `unavailableDecisions`, and the derived `allowAlwaysUnavailableReason` together. Prompt renderers consume that source-of-truth metadata instead of guessing from a missing button, while schema validation and normalization keep older requests compatible when the explicit field is absent.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The canonical boundary remains request construction and validation, not individual UI strings. The gateway schema accepts the additive nullable reason, the server derives it from existing request fields, and renderers only map that normalized contract to copy. No migration, default policy, or persistence-store change is required.
- `ask=always` still wins over stale explicit reasons, so policy-required approval continues to use the policy explanation.
- `unavailableDecisions: ["allow-always"]` under `ask=on-miss` now derives the one-shot explanation when an explicit reason is absent.

## Changes

- Added centralized exec approval copy/reason helpers for `policy-ask-always`, `one-shot-command`, and generic unavailable cases.
- Added request-scoped `allowAlwaysUnavailableReason` metadata and propagated it through:
  - gateway request creation and `exec.approval.get`
  - host/node approval registration and pending tool results
  - runtime, reply, forwarder, and embedded-agent approval prompts
  - approval view models and plugin reaction/manual fallback paths
  - native Matrix, Telegram, and iMessage approval surfaces
  - control UI parsing/rendering fallback
- Updated gateway protocol validation to accept known reason values or `null`, and regenerated the Swift protocol model.
- Added regression tests for request reason resolution, gateway validation, metadata propagation, policy-vs-one-shot copy, UI fallback behavior, and Matrix structured metadata.
- Public contract scope is additive and backward-compatible: older clients can omit the reason, send `null`, or rely on the server-derived fallback from `ask` and `unavailableDecisions`.
- Related open PR / same-contract scan was treated as background only; no related open PR was used to supersede or broaden this issue flow.
- Out of scope: changing approval policy semantics, adding new allowlist persistence patterns for redirected shell commands, changing command parsing, or changing non-exec/plugin approval behavior.

## Real behavior proof

- **Real environment tested:** Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2019 via Git Bash, Node v22.17.0, pnpm 11.2.2. The focused tests exercise the real prompt/reply/view-model builders used by gateway, runtime, UI, and chat/native approval paths.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-approval-unavailable-copy.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-request.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/infra/approval-view-model.test.ts src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts src/infra/exec-approval-reply.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/exec-approvals-validators.test.ts ui/src/ui/controllers/exec-approval.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/exec-approval.test.ts extensions/matrix/src/approval-handler.runtime.test.ts
```

```text
node --import tsx scripts/protocol-gen-swift.ts
git diff --check
```

```text
OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false pnpm check:changed
```

- **Evidence after fix:** The focused approval regression run exited 0. Protocol generation exited 0 and rewrote the Swift model from the schema. `git diff --check` exited 0. The changed-file check passed the guard/typecheck/lint lanes before reaching the platform-specific macOS app CI lane.
- **Observed result after fix:** Regression assertions now verify that `ask=always` renders `The effective approval policy requires approval every time, so Allow Always is unavailable.`, while `ask=on-miss` with `unavailableDecisions: ["allow-always"]` renders `Allow Always is unavailable because this command is one-shot and cannot be saved as a reusable approval.` The allowed replies/buttons omit `allow-always` in both unavailable cases.
- **What was not tested:** The `macOS app CI tests` lane did not complete successfully on this Windows Git Bash host. That lane was triggered by the generated Swift protocol model update under `apps/shared/OpenClawKit`; failures were in macOS packaging/signing script harness tests with Windows/Git Bash path-format differences and local Corepack/pnpm availability inside the harness. Remote macOS CI should provide authoritative coverage for that lane.

## Evidence

The focused approval regression command completed successfully with exit code 0.

The local changed-file command reported these lanes as passing before the macOS packaging-script lane:

```text
ok conflict markers
ok changelog attributions
ok guarded extension wildcard re-exports
ok plugin-sdk wildcard re-exports
ok duplicate scan target coverage
ok dependency pin guard
ok package patch guard
ok test temp creation report
ok typecheck core
ok typecheck core tests
ok typecheck extensions
ok typecheck extension tests
ok lint core
ok lint extensions
ok lint apps (swiftlint unavailable on this host)
failed: macOS app CI tests
```

The macOS app CI failures were local host/tooling failures in packaging/signing harness tests, not approval-flow assertion failures. Representative failure modes were path-format mismatches between Windows paths and Git Bash `/c/...` paths, plus Corepack/pnpm availability inside the spawned packaging harness.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/infra/exec-approval-unavailable-copy.test.ts` covers the new source-of-truth reason resolution. Additional regression coverage is in gateway, runtime, reply/forwarder, view-model, plugin reaction, UI controller/view, protocol validator, host registration, and Matrix approval handler tests.
- **Scenario locked in:** The regression scenario locks `ask=on-miss` plus `unavailableDecisions: ["allow-always"]` for a redirected/non-persistable command shape and asserts the prompt offers only `allow-once|deny` with the one-shot copy. A separate policy scenario locks `ask=always` to the policy copy.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The tests call the shared resolver, request registration, protocol validator, and prompt builders directly, so each source-of-truth and propagation boundary is covered without adding a brittle full end-to-end approval workflow fixture.
- Policy case: `ask=always` hides `Allow Always` and keeps the policy explanation.
- One-shot case: `ask=on-miss` plus `unavailableDecisions: ["allow-always"]` hides `Allow Always` and renders the one-shot/non-persistable explanation.
- Compatibility case: missing explicit reason is derived from existing request fields.
- Protocol case: schema accepts `policy-ask-always`, `one-shot-command`, `unavailable`, and `null`, while rejecting unknown reason strings.
- Surface propagation case: gateway, pending replies, native/chat approval metadata, and UI prompts preserve the unavailable metadata.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk:contract`, `merge-risk:ui`, `merge-risk:extensions`, `merge-risk:generated-protocol`.
- **Risk explanation:** This is additive metadata, but it crosses public/wire-ish approval surfaces and generated protocol models. The main risk is a surface forgetting to forward the reason and falling back to generic/policy copy.
- **Why acceptable:** The gateway derives the reason from existing fields when explicit metadata is missing; `ask=always` takes precedence for safety; unknown reason strings normalize away; protocol validation allows `null` for compatibility; tests cover the affected prompt and metadata surfaces.
- **Patch quality notes:** Patch-quality warnings were reviewed. The added default returns are normalization exits for invalid/no metadata and for the valid case where `allow-always` is available; they do not mask a denial path. The fallback wording appears in regression tests that verify request fallback behavior. The public contract risk is bounded to an additive nullable schema field. The large diff is mostly propagation across existing approval surfaces so every renderer uses the same request-scoped source of truth instead of recreating policy guesses.

target.body:
fix(memory): incremental session sync;fix bugs;move to extensions:memory-core (openclaw#40919) (openclaw#59577)

## Summary

Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets:

If this PR fixes a plugin beta-release blocker, title it `fix(<plugin-id>): beta blocker - <summary>` and link the matching `Beta blocker: <plugin-name> - <summary>` issue labeled `beta-blocker`. Contributors cannot label PRs, so the title is the PR-side signal for maintainers and automation.

- **Problem**: When a session file grows, the memory index performs a full reindex - deleting all chunks, re-generating all content, re-computing all embeddings, and re-inserting everything. This causes O(n) performance degradation as sessions grow longer.
- **Why it matters**: Each 1.5 seconds of session growth triggers a full reindex. For a 50-turn session with 10 chunks, this means 10 embedding API calls every time, even when only 1-2 new chunks were added. This wastes API quota, increases latency, and causes unnecessary database writes.
- **What changed**: Implement hash-based incremental indexing for session files. Only new or changed chunks are re-embedded, while unchanged chunks are preserved. This reduces embedding API calls by 28-67% depending on session growth.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary)**: Memory files (MEMORY.md) still use full reindex. Only session files use incremental sync. The chunking algorithm is unchanged. The embedding provider is unchanged.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable)

For bug fixes or regressions, explain why this happened, not just what changed. Otherwise write `N/A`. If the cause is unclear, write `Unknown`.

N/A - This is a feature, not a bug fix.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

For bug fixes or regressions, name the smallest reliable test coverage that should have caught this. Otherwise write `N/A`.

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [ ] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `manager.incremental-session.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: Session growth triggers incremental sync instead of full reindex
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly tests the hash-based deduplication logic
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): `manager.atomic-reindex.test.ts` covers full reindex
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

List user-visible changes (including defaults/config).  
If none, write `None`.

None. The incremental sync is transparent to users. Session syncs are faster but the behavior is identical.

## Diagram (if applicable)

For UI changes or non-trivial logic flows, include a small ASCII diagram reviewers can scan quickly. Otherwise write `N/A`.

```text
Before (Full Reindex):
[session grows] -> [delete ALL chunks] -> [regenerate ALL chunks] -> [embed ALL chunks] -> [insert ALL chunks]

After (Incremental Sync):
[session grows] -> [generate ALL chunks] -> [compare hashes] -> [skip unchanged] -> [embed NEW chunks only] -> [insert NEW chunks only]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`No`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux (Fedora)
- Runtime/container: Node.js 22
- Model/provider: Ollama + nomic-embed-text
- Integration/channel: Session memory sync
- Relevant config (redacted):
  ```json
  {
    "memory": {
      "sources": ["sessions"],
      "chunking": { "tokens": 200, "overlap": 50 },
      "experimental": { "sessionMemory": true }
    }
  }
  ```

### Steps

1. Create a session with 3 turns (6 messages)
2. Run initial sync with `force: true`
3. Grow session to 5 turns (+2 turns = +4 messages)
4. Run incremental sync with `sessionFiles: [path]`
5. Verify that only 1 chunk was re-embedded (not all 3)

### Expected

- Incremental sync embeds only new/changed chunks
- Existing chunks are preserved with identical embeddings
- Embedding API calls reduced by 50-67%

### Actual

- Confirmed: Only 1 chunk re-embedded (vs 3 with full reindex)
- Confirmed: Existing chunks have byte-for-byte identical embeddings
- Measured: 50-67% reduction in embedding calls

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Perf numbers (if relevant)

### Benchmark Results (Real Ollama API)

| Scenario | Chunks Before | Chunks After | Full Reindex | Incremental | Saving |
|----------|---------------|--------------|--------------|-------------|--------|
| overlap=0, +2 turns | 2 | 3 | 3 calls | 1 call | **66.7%** |
| overlap=0, +5 turns | 3 | 5 | 5 calls | 2 calls | **60.0%** |
| overlap=50, +2 turns | 2 | 4 | 4 calls | 2 calls | **50.0%** |
| overlap=50, +5 turns | 4 | 9 | 9 calls | 5 calls | **44.4%** |

### Embedding Consistency Verification

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| Full reindex twice (same content) | ✅ Identical embeddings |
| Incremental sync preserves embeddings | ✅ Byte-for-byte identical |
| Full reindex after incremental | ✅ Identical embeddings |

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios:
  - Session growth with overlap=0
  - Session growth with overlap=50
  - Unicode content preservation
  - Long messages (multiple chunks per message)
  - Very long sessions (50+ turns)
- Edge cases checked:
  - Empty file → single message
  - Single message → multiple messages
  - Large chunks (all content in one chunk)
- What you did **not** verify:
  - Real-world production sessions with actual user data
  - Performance on very large sessions (100+ turns)

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [ ] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

### Compatibility Details

| Aspect | Status | Details |
|--------|--------|---------|
| Database Schema | ✅ Compatible | Uses `ensureColumn()` to safely add new columns with default values |
| API Compatibility | ✅ Compatible | `indexFile()` preserved, `indexSessionFileIncremental()` is new |
| Existing Data | ✅ Compatible | Existing chunks work normally, new columns default to 0 |
| Downgrade | ✅ Compatible | Old versions ignore new columns, still function correctly |

## Risks and Mitigations

List only real risks for this PR. Add/remove entries as needed. If none, write `None`.

- **Risk**: Existing chunks have `start_offset=0, end_offset=0` which may cause hash lookup issues
  - **Mitigation**: Hash-based lookup ignores offset values, uses content hash for matching

- **Risk**: Single-chunk sessions don't benefit from incremental sync
  - **Mitigation**: This is expected behavior - small sessions naturally re-embed all content. No regression compared to before.

- **Risk**: Overlap causes boundary chunks to change, reducing hash preservation rate
  - **Mitigation**: This is inherent to the overlap mechanism. Users can reduce overlap to improve preservation rate.

target.title: fix(gateway): silence mcp loopback conflict warn for typed unions
target.body:
## Summary

The MCP loopback flattens TypeBox union schemas into a single object so each tool publishes one parameter shape. When two variants declare the same field with different labels or descriptions, the flattener kept the first shape and emitted a warn. With many local tools using `Type.Union([Type.Object(...)])`, that warn fired on every tool listing and drowned real diagnostics.

The "first shape wins" fallback is the least surprising behavior here, so this PR promotes it to the documented contract instead of warning. Adds a regression test to lock the silent behavior in.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test src/gateway/mcp-http.schema.test.ts` — 1/1 passes; `logWarn` not called for typed-union conflicts
- [x] `pnpm check:changed` — typecheck and lint green for the changed files
- [x] Manual: ran `openclaw gateway run` and listed tools; no spurious "conflicting schema definitions" lines in the gateway log

target.title: fix(control-ui): show archived transcripts and images after reset
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #77819. After a session reset, the prior `.jsonl.reset.<ts>` and
`.jsonl.deleted.<ts>` transcripts persisted on disk but were unreachable
from the Control UI, so the conversation and its image attachments
looked deleted even though the data was retained.

- **Gateway**: enumerate archived transcripts in the agent's sessions
  directory and attach an `archivedTranscripts` summary to the agent's
  main session row in `sessions.list`. Add two additive RPCs under the
  read scope:
  - `sessions.archived.list` — lists archived transcripts (filename,
    archivedAt, reason, sessionId, sizeBytes, agentId).
  - `sessions.archived.read` — reads a specific archived transcript's
    messages by filename. Validates the resolved path stays inside the
    agent's sessions dir (path-traversal guard) and that the filename
    matches the `<sessionId>.jsonl.(reset|deleted).<isoTs>` shape.
- **Control UI**: render archived transcripts in the session row's
  expanded panel with an inline viewer. The viewer renders text, image,
  and attachment content blocks from the JSONL, so prior image
  attachments come back as soon as you open one — no separate route
  or download needed.

Image attachments were never deleted; they were stored in the archived
JSONL and just had no UI surface. The new viewer reads the same blocks
the live chat view consumes, including base64 `image/*` sources.

## Affected surfaces

- `sessions.list` payload: each agent main row may now carry
  `archivedTranscripts: ArchivedTranscriptPreview[]` (additive).
- New RPCs `sessions.archived.list` / `sessions.archived.read`
  (read-scoped, additive — third-party clients are unaffected).
- Control UI Sessions tab: row expansion now triggers when archived
  transcripts exist, even without compaction checkpoints.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** After `sessions.reset`, archived `.jsonl.reset.<ts>` transcripts persisted in the agent sessions directory but were unreachable from the Control UI, so the prior conversation and its image attachments looked deleted. This change attaches `archivedTranscripts` to the agent's main session row in `sessions.list` and adds two read-scope Gateway RPCs (`sessions.archived.list`, `sessions.archived.read`) that the Sessions view consumes to render archived transcripts inline. Fixes #77819.

- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.14.0, pnpm 10.33.2. OpenClaw built from this branch via `pnpm build` (commit `76f6758`). Gateway run via `node openclaw.mjs --dev gateway run --port 19001` (loopback bind, token auth, dev profile under `~/.openclaw-dev`).

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `pnpm install && pnpm build`
  2. `node openclaw.mjs --dev gateway run --port 19001` (background)
  3. Wrote a synthetic archived transcript at `~/.openclaw-dev/agents/dev/sessions/a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d.jsonl.reset.2026-05-05T10-00-00.000Z` with a user message containing a text block + a base64 `image/png` block, and an assistant reply. Standard archive shape produced by `sessions.reset` per `src/gateway/session-transcript-files.fs.ts`.
  4. Called the two new RPCs and `sessions.list` against the running gateway via `openclaw --dev gateway call <method> --params '<json>' --json`.
  5. Called `sessions.archived.read` with a path-traversal filename to confirm rejection.

- **Evidence after fix:**

  ```text
  $ openclaw --version
  OpenClaw 2026.5.4 (76f6758)

  $ ls -la ~/.openclaw-dev/agents/dev/sessions/
  -rw------- 1 root root  691 May  5 20:31 a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d.jsonl.reset.2026-05-05T10-00-00.000Z
  -rw------- 1 root root 4263 May  5 20:08 sessions.json

  ===== sessions.archived.list =====
  $ openclaw --dev gateway call sessions.archived.list --params '{"agentId":"dev"}' --json
  {
    "archived": [
      {
        "archivedFileName": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d.jsonl.reset.2026-05-05T10-00-00.000Z",
  ```

target.title: fix(gateway): add max reconnect limit with opt-in maxReconnectAttempts
target.body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in reconnect attempt limit for GatewayClient to prevent infinite reconnect loops in short-lived clients (gateway CLI, MCP bridge, etc.).

Resolves #45469

## Changes

- Add `maxReconnectAttempts?: number` to `GatewayClientOptions`
- When set, `scheduleReconnect()` gives up after N attempts and fires `onReconnectPaused` with `detailCode: null`
- When unset (default), behavior is unchanged — unlimited retries, preserving node-host recovery semantics
- Reset `reconnectAttempts` counter on successful hello-ok handshake
- Two tests: cap exhaustion + counter reset after recovery

## Why opt-in

Node-host relies on GatewayClient retrying indefinitely during gateway outages. A global cap would zombie node-host processes. Making it opt-in means node-host is unchanged while CLI/bridge callers can opt in to bounded retries.

## Test plan

- [x] Stops after N reconnect attempts and fires onReconnectPaused
- [x] Counter resets on successful connect
- [x] CI green (lint, type-check, security, boundaries)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** GatewayClient reconnects infinitely with no upper bound on attempts. After applying this patch, callers can opt in to a bounded reconnect limit via `maxReconnectAttempts` while node-host retains unbounded retries.

**Real environment tested:** ARM64 Linux (aarch64, Ubuntu), Node.js v22.22.2, running vitest against patched `src/gateway/client.ts` from `fix/max-reconnect-limit-v2` branch.

**Exact steps or command run after the patch:** Ran targeted reconnect tests: `npx vitest run src/gateway/client.test.ts -t "reconnect" --reporter=verbose`

- **Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):**


**Observed result after fix:** With `maxReconnectAttempts: 30` set, the client fires `onReconnectPaused({ code: -1, reason: "max reconnect attempts reached (30)", detailCode: null })` after 30 failures and stops reconnecting. After a successful hello-ok handshake the counter resets, allowing another full cycle. Without the option set, reconnects continue unbounded — no behavior change.

**Not tested:** Full end-to-end reconnect against a live gateway server (no local gateway instance available on this ARM host).

target.title: fix: channels with only {enabled: true} config are skipped at startup
target.body:
## Problem

`hasMeaningfulChannelConfig` in `src/channels/config-presence.ts` filters out channel configs that only contain `{"enabled": true}`. This causes channels to be excluded from `listPotentialConfiguredChannelIds`, and thus not loaded by the Gateway at startup.

`qqbot` channel works because it also has `appId` and `clientSecret` keys. But any channel that only sets `enabled: true` is silently skipped.

## Fix

Added early return `if (value.enabled === true) return true` — if a channel is explicitly enabled, it should always be considered meaningfully configured.

## Before/After

| Config | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| `{"enabled": true}` | ❌ skipped | ✅ loaded |
| `{"enabled": true, "appId": "x"}` | ✅ loaded | ✅ loaded |
| `{"enabled": false}` | ❌ skipped | ❌ skipped |
| `{}` | ❌ skipped | ❌ skipped |

## Summary

- add a small one-shot CLI exit helper for default-runtime inspection commands
- call it after successful `models list` and `models status` output paths

## Why

On my live VPS running OpenClaw 2026.5.4, several non-interactive model inspection commands printed complete output but did not terminate. This makes scripts and SSH diagnostics hit their timeout even though the command already produced the requested data.

- Real environment tested: OpenClaw source checkout on macOS, running the patched CLI with a temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME`; before-fix behavior was reproduced on my live VPS with OpenClaw 2026.5.4.

target.title: fix(memory-core): clean stale short-term temp files
target.body:
## Summary

- clean stale orphaned `short-term-recall.json.*.tmp` and `phase-signals.json.*.tmp` files during short-term promotion repair
- preserve fresh temp files and unrelated temp-looking files so active or manual files are not swept
- surface `removedTempFiles` through memory-core repair summaries, doctor output, and the plugin SDK facade

Fixes #77888.

## Root cause

`writeStore` and `writePhaseSignalStore` write a sibling temp file and then rename it into place. A process crash or failed rename after the write can leave the temp file in `memory/.dreams` indefinitely because repair only normalized the recall store and stale lock.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: stale orphaned memory-core short-term recall temp files are removed by repair, while fresh temp files and unrelated temp-looking files are preserved.
- Real environment tested: local OpenClaw checkout on macOS with Node running the patched memory-core repair function against a temporary OpenClaw workspace under `/var/folders/.../T`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: ran `node --import tsx` from the patched checkout, created a temporary workspace, wrote an old matching `short-term-recall.json.*.tmp`, a fresh matching temp file, and an unrelated `.manual.tmp`, then called `repairShortTermPromotionArtifacts({ workspaceDir })`.
- Evidence after fix: copied live terminal output from the command:

```json
{
  "workspaceDir": "/var/folders/cf/mtzn4vhx6kz_83fmvt5qs60m0000gn/T/openclaw-77888-proof-tf7V6a",
  "changed": true,
  "removedTempFiles": 1,
  "rewroteStore": false,
  "removedStaleLock": false,
  "oldTmpExists": false,
  "freshTmpExists": true,

}
```

- What was not tested: I did not force-kill a live dreaming process mid-rename; the live proof exercised the repair cleanup path directly with the same temp-file naming pattern left by interrupted atomic writes.
